37.0.0.en: 1 Every friend saith, "I also am his friend": but there is a friend which is only a friend in name. Is it not a grief unto death, 2 when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy? 3 O wicked imagination, whence camest thou in to cover the dry land with deceit? 4 There is a companion which rejoiceth in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble he will be against him. 5 There is a companion which for the belly's sake laboureth with his friend, and taketh up the buckler against the enemy. 6 Forget not thy friend in thy mind, and be not unmindful of him in thy riches. 7 Consult not with him that suspecteth thee, and hide thy counsel from such as envy thee. 8 Every counsellor extolleth counsel, but some counsel for themselves.

37.0.1.en: Sirach returns to speak about friends, who must be faithful and chosen with a spirit of discernment, offering examples of those who must be avoided:

37.0.2.en: A. Those who are friends in name only, without deeds (nominalism); that is, their friendship is not genuine [1].

37.1.0.en: B. The friend who may turn into an enemy, and who is worse than the enemy who is open from the beginning [2]. The bad example in the Bible is Judas the traitor. He is a deceiver [3]. Such a friend leaves a bad mark on the lives of many, for he stirs up suspicion among some friends. The appearance of such a person drives some to examine seriously the motives of the one with whom they will be joined as a friend.

37.1.1.en: C. A friend who is not steadfast in his friendship, who clings to his friend in his prosperity and ignores him in his adversity. Sometimes he even takes up toward him an attitude of enmity without any real cause.

37.1.2.en: D. There are friends whose friendship stops at the limits of courtesies, especially in holding banquets and parties on occasions.

37.1.3.en: Sirach gives a person advice so that he may practise genuine friendship, by being concerned with his friend as one who dwells in his depths, caring for him and supporting him even materially.

37.1.4.en: Every friend says: "I also am your friend," but sometimes he is a friend in name only [1].

37.1.5.en: Ben Sira begins the list of those to be rejected from friendship with those who claim friendship but do not practise it in deed. Some, without discernment, are occupied with the number of friends around them, not with their quality. The heart of the believer must open itself in love, if possible, to everyone, but not everyone is a friend to whom he discloses his secrets, for at some time they may wrong him, and they may even destroy him.

37.1.6.en: Is it not a grief unto death when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy? [2]

37.1.7.en: The second group is the unfaithful persons who for some hidden reason turn from friendship to enmity. Examples of this are Judas, to whom the Lord Christ gave many blessings, but because of his love of silver he betrayed his Master; and also King Saul, whom the boy David rescued, and when the people loved the boy, he set it in his heart to be rid of him by every means. In contrast to this is the character of David, who met Saul's enmity with love and would not accept to take vengeance on him, but even kept friendship with Saul and his offspring after Saul's death.

37.1.8.en: It is exceedingly sad when a friend in name, in whom his friend trusts, turns into an enemy to him.

37.2.0.en: O wicked thought! Why were you drawn in to cover the earth with deceit? [3]

37.2.1.en: Ben Sira stands grieved at what has befallen the nature of man, which God created good and possessed of authority, how it has been brought low by sin and evil inclinations have crept over it. And man, created in the image of God, has turned from being a friend to his brethren into an enemy! These evil inclinations do not harm the person himself alone, but the fallen nature of man. The Apostle says: "For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope" (Rom 8:20). St. John Chrysostom sees that corruption has come down not only upon the nature of man but upon creation as well. And when the nature of man is restored by the work of the Savior, the world is delivered from the bondage of corruption (Rom 8:21), for he says:

37.2.2.en: [Now, what is this creation? It does not mean you alone, but with you also the lower creation, which does not share with you in reason or sense; this shares your blessings. He says: "It shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption," that is, it will no longer become corrupt, but will walk side by side with the beauty that is given to your body. For just as when your body became corrupt it also became corrupt, so now, when your body becomes incorruptible, it also follows it. And as the Apostle declares this he reaches the conclusion: "into the glorious liberty of the children of God," so that its freedom is fulfilled.

37.2.3.en: He is like a nurse who is bringing up a king's son: when the son receives his father's authority she enjoys the good things with him, and so it is also with creation together with us. You see that in all things man occupies the position of leadership, for it is for his sake that all things were made. Behold how (the Apostle) soothes the wrestler, showing God's unspeakable love toward man, for he wishes to say: Why are you troubled at your trials? For if you suffer for your own sake, even creation suffers because of you. And he not only soothes, but also shows that what he utters is a matter of importance. For if creation, which was brought into being wholly for your sake, is "in hope," how much more does it befit you to be in hope, you through whom creation will enjoy those good things? Just as fathers, when they see their sons on the way to receiving an honor, clothe the servants in splendid garments for the glory of the son, so God clothes creation with incorruption for the glory of the freedom of the sons[1].]

37.2.4.en: Man abused the emotions that God gave him, and also the gift of reasoning and true wisdom, and so man fell into treachery, which appeared clearly in Cain, who killed his brother Abel because he was more righteous than he.

37.3.0.en: There is a companion who rejoices at the joy of a friend, but in the time of affliction he is against him [4].

37.3.1.en: The third group that must be avoided is the person who exploits his brother: he befriends him where he gains a personal benefit, and is hostile to him when he finds no personal benefit in him.

37.4.0.en: There is a companion who strives to help a friend for the sake of his belly, and in the time of battle he takes up the shield [5].

37.4.1.en: The fourth group, persons whose dealings are limited to parties and amusement, and who care neither for the salvation of their own souls nor for the salvation of their families and friends.

37.4.2.en: Do not forget your friend within your soul[2], and do not neglect him when you distribute your wealth [6].

37.4.3.en: After warning us against the four preceding groups, he called us to be faithful friends ourselves. The mark of true friendship is that our friend has a special place in our souls, that is, in our hearts, thought and feelings, and that we count what we possess as a divine gift with which we support others.

37.5.0.en: 9 Beware of the counsellor, and first inquire what he needs; for he will counsel what profits himself, 10 lest he cast the lot upon you, and say to you: 11 "Your way is good," and then stand over against you to see what will befall you. 12 Do not consult the hypocrite about godliness, nor the unjust man about justice, nor a woman about her rival, nor a coward about war, nor a merchant about trade, nor a buyer about selling, nor the envious man about giving thanks for kindness, 13 nor the harsh man about tenderness, nor the slothful man about any work, 14 nor the hired man who lives with you about finishing work, nor the idler about much work. Do not give heed to these in any matter of counsel. 15 But keep company with the godly man, whom you know to keep the commandments, 16 whose soul is as your soul, and who, when you fall, grieves for you. 17 And establish counsel with the heart, for you have no counsellor more faithful than it, 18 for a man's soul sometimes tells the truth more than seven watchmen who watch from a high place. 19 And in all these things pray to the Most High, that He may guide you in truth in the straight way.

37.5.1.en: The counsellor is more serious than the friend, for what a person asks of a friend is that he share his sufferings and joys and not divulge his secrets. But the counsellor, besides what pertains to the faithful friend of these qualities, is wise and marked by a spirit of discernment, so that a person may ask counsel of him, especially in taking a decision that is fateful in his life.

37.6.0.en: On the positive side, the friend or counsellor must be chosen godly, keeping the commandments, and concerned for his own salvation and the salvation of the one whose friend or counsellor he is [12].

37.6.1.en: Sirach stresses an important element in all matters, especially in choosing the friend and counsellor, and that is prayer to God, the searcher of hearts, who knows the depths of every person.

37.6.2.en: Every counsellor extols his counsel, and some give counsel for their own benefit [7].

37.6.3.en: Ben Sira directs our gaze to the one who claims wisdom and experience in managing affairs and in guiding the one who consults him to the sound choice. Yet he is selfish and pretends concern and love, while what occupies him in the decision he advises to the one who consults him is that it should be beneficial to himself, whether materially, psychologically or socially, without caring for the losses that the one who sought his counsel will reap.

37.6.4.en: Guard yourself against the counsellor, and know beforehand his interest.

37.6.5.en: For he will think of himself, lest he cast the lot against you [8].

37.6.6.en: Before a person chooses his friend, he must observe and study what his interests are, whether he has a heart wide with love for those with whom he deals, lest the person be surprised one day that he is advising him to his own harm.

37.6.7.en: Casting the lot here is meant as harboring evil so that the harm falls upon the friend.

37.6.8.en: And he says to you: "Your way is good," then stands aside to see what will befall you [9].

37.6.9.en: Do not make one who is suspicious of you your counsellor, and at the same time it is fitting that you hide your secrets from the one who envies you. By this he has warned us in general against those who are marked by the following: those who care for their own good and are indifferent to the interest of others, those who gloat over others' misfortune, those whom a person suspects, and those who envy him for what he has.

37.6.10.en: Now he presents to us certain groups that must be avoided when choosing a counsellor:

37.6.11.en: Do not consult a man who looks at you with suspicion, and hide your counsel from those who envy you [10].

37.6.12.en: Do not consult a woman about her rival, nor a coward about the battle, nor a merchant about exchange, nor a buyer about selling, nor a slanderer about gratitude, nor an unmerciful man about generosity, nor an idle man about any work, nor a seasonal hireling about finishing his work.

37.6.13.en: Nor a slothful servant about a great work, so do not listen to these in any counsel [11].

37.6.14.en: Here wisdom warns us against choosing the counsellor from one of the preceding groups.

37.6.15.en: A. Do not consult the wife about her rival [11], for her opinion of her is known beforehand; she will not sympathize with her, but heaps accusations and faults upon her.

37.6.16.en: B. A soldier in a battle must not consult one who is known to be a coward [11], for he weakens hearts and discourages resolve, since he has no ability to face the enemy.

37.6.17.en: C. One must not seek the counsel of a greedy merchant when he wants to barter with another [11], nor must a seller seek the counsel of the one who buys from him [11]. For what concerns them both is that the deal should go to themselves, so both are biased, and neither will be impartial in his advice.

37.6.18.en: D. One must not consult a slanderer whom he does not trust with his secret. For such a counsellor himself is not faithful with the secrets of others. This is what happened with wicked Haman when King Ahasuerus consulted him about Mordecai, and how he should reward him for the good he had done him; Haman bore a grudge against Mordecai, but his evil turned back upon his own head.

37.6.19.en: E. A person must not consult someone about a matter that he is unable to carry out: he must not ask giving of one who is a counsellor without mercy, nor ask the slothful about any work he wishes to complete, nor ask one who seeks a wage for seasonal work about finishing his work.

37.6.20.en: Instead of this, persevere with the godly man, whom you know to keep the commandments, whose soul agrees with your soul, and who, if you fall, shares your sufferings [12].

37.6.21.en: After Ben Sira has given advice about avoiding choosing as friends those unfit to give good and fitting counsel, he gives positive advice in choosing the friend. First, that he himself be godly, keeping the divine commandment, and that he choose a friend who agrees with him in godliness and the keeping of the commandments. Second, that he be loving and self-giving, sharing his sufferings. So his counsellor must not be one of those who love frivolity without seriousness, and he must not be a drunkard.

37.6.22.en: v It is impossible for you to become good or wise in a moment; rather you need study, care, exercise, training and long striving (and above all) a strong desire for the good.

37.6.23.en: The good man who loves God and who truly knows God never ceases to do, without exception, all the things that please God. But it is rare that we meet such people[3].

37.7.0.en: St. Anthony the Great v Let us keep away, keep far away from joking, for it is the beginning of the use of abuse; through it dangerous quarrels and growing enmities break out. In our opinion arrogance accompanies drunkenness. A man is condemned not only for his deeds but also for his words. The Scripture says: "Reprove not thy neighbour at the wine, ... and speak not unto him words of reproach" [31]. Surely we were strongly counselled to keep company with the godly man [12]; therefore he who makes sport of a holy man commits a sin[4].

37.7.1.en: St. Clement of Alexandria And hold fast to the counsel of your heart, for there is none more faithful to you than it [13].

37.7.2.en: Ben Sira wishes to direct his disciples to their depths, so that their hearts may be sanctified in the Lord and be more faithful to them than friends and counsellors. It is dangerous to think that humility and seeking counsel mean that a person should behave in a spirit of weakness and lack of confidence in himself. For God created man to be a leader in the Lord.

37.7.3.en: When the Lord Christ became a boy of twelve years, He affirmed His leading role by saying to St. Mary: "Wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" (Lk 2:49). He spent three days in the temple and was sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them and asking them questions, and all who heard Him were astonished at His understanding and answers. This conduct is counted a revolution in the world of boys, so we do not belittle them, but respect their mission, their personalities, their potentials and their role.

37.7.4.en: For a man's soul sometimes tells him more than seven watchmen sitting high on a watchtower [14].

37.7.5.en: Solomon the Wise stands in amazement before the wisdom of the Creator, which is manifested in raising man up as a leader to rule over the world. For he says: "And ordained man through thy wisdom, that he should have dominion over the creatures which thou hast made, and order the world according to equity and righteousness, and execute judgment with an upright heart" (Wis 9:2-3). Before we seek the support of any man, whatever his abilities, wisdom and love, we must trust in what God has given us of grace and ability to cling to Him, and ask for His leading of us, but not in arrogance and haughtiness, rather in humility and living faith.

37.7.6.en: And in all cases pray to the Most High, that He may direct your way in truth [15].

37.7.7.en: If God calls us to have fathers as leaders and wise counsellors, then let God be first in all our decisions.

37.7.8.en: The Apostle Paul presents himself as an example not only for bishops and priests, but for every true believer, for he says: "We are fools for Christ's sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong; ye are honourable, but we are despised" (1 Cor 4:10). The Apostle finds his delight in being counted a fool for the sake of Christ the Lover of mankind, and counts those he serves as wise in Christ.

37.8.0.en: 20 A word is the beginning of every work, and counsel goes before every action. 21 The countenance shows the changing of the heart. Four things proceed from the heart: good and evil, life and death, and that which rules over these at all times is the tongue. 22 There is one among men who is shrewd, a teacher of many, but he profits his own soul nothing. 23 And there is one who claims wisdom, and his speech is hated. Such a one shall be deprived of all food, 24 for he has not been given favour from the Lord, since he has no share of wisdom. 25 And there is one whose wisdom is for himself, and the fruits of his understanding are good in the mouth. 26 The wise man teaches his people, and the fruits of his understanding are good. 27 The wise man is filled with blessing, and all who see him count him happy. 28 The life of a man is numbered days, but the days of Israel have no number. 29 The wise man inherits the confidence of his people, and his name lives forever. 30 My son, test your soul in your life, and see what harms it, and keep it from that. 31 For not everything is profitable for everyone, nor is every soul pleased with everything.

37.8.1.en: A word is the beginning of every work, and counsel goes before every action [16].

37.8.2.en: The word meant here is not that which is spoken by the tongue, but that which the mind and heart adopt. Thinking precedes the work, and the expression of it decides the fate of man, the life of man or his death. "By thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned" (Mt 12:37). So man's life and death are in his speech. "Death and life are in the power of the tongue" (Prov 18:21). And counsel also must precede the work.

37.8.3.en: v O brother, the Holy Scripture says: "Do all things with counsel" [Prov 24:72 (a) according to the text], and "Without counsel do nothing" (b). When you acted without counsel, but by your own will, you were not striving with your mind. For there is none who has no need of counsel except God alone, who created wisdom; but when you sought to cut off your own will according to God and to reach humility, and to take me, your very little brother, as a guide, you aroused the envy of Satan, the enemy of good, who envies all men continually[5].

37.8.4.en: v If you are dead to the flesh, how can the natural passions be alive in you? But if you have not yet reached spiritual perfection but are still carnal, and if you are still a little child in the Spirit, then lay yourself down (that is, humble yourself) in the Spirit and submit yourself to a teacher so that he may discipline you with mercy. "Do nothing without counsel" (see Sir 32:19), even if things seem good to you, for the light of the demons becomes darkness in the end. If you hear or think or see anything that leaves even a little disturbance in your heart, know that it is from the demons[6].

37.8.5.en: St. Barsanuphius Four kinds of things appear as a sign of the changing of the heart [17].

37.8.6.en: Good and evil; life and death.

37.8.7.en: And the tongue is the one that rules over these at all times [18].

37.8.8.en: It befits the mind to take its fateful decision from four choices: good, evil, life and death.

37.8.9.en: There is a clever man who is a teacher of many, but he does not profit his own soul [19].

37.8.10.en: There are among men those who are clever, able to teach by word, but their lives nullify what they say.

37.8.11.en: v For a man's words to be convincing, the life of the speaker has a great effect, more than any loftiness of eloquence, no matter how eloquent[7].

37.8.12.en: St. Augustine v A good example gives a sweeter and more pleasant voice than the sounds of music and all instruments of entertainment, for people do not weigh what we say as much as what we do.

37.8.13.en: St. John Chrysostom The man who invents crafty words will be hated; this man will go away hungry [20].

37.8.14.en: St. Augustine translates it: "He who speaks sophistically is hated," and comments on it, saying: [In any case, the person may not be a deceiver, but he is concerned with adorning speech literally, in a sort of exaggeration and not in earnest, so that his speech is counted sophistical[8].]

37.8.15.en: v A man ought to be purified before he purifies others, and become wise so that he may make them wise, and a light to shine upon them, and draw near to God to draw them to God, and be sanctified for the sake of their sanctification, and have someone to lead him so that he may himself lead them with wisdom.

37.9.0.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Grace has not been given to him from the Lord, for he is deprived of all wisdom [21].

37.9.1.en: If we do not care to enjoy God's wisdom, we shall not experience His grace in our lives.

37.10.0.en: And there is a man who is wise to himself, and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy when he speaks [22].

37.10.1.en: It is good that a person's life be a practical lesson, but there is a need for the word by which he expresses his life.

37.11.0.en: The wise man teaches his people, and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy [23].

37.11.1.en: It befits the wise man to teach, for his life proves what he proclaims, so that people trust him.

37.12.0.en: The wise man is full of blessing, and all who see him count him blessed [24].

37.12.1.en: What people perceive in the life of the wise man is not only his wise conduct and godliness but also the blessing of the Lord tangibly present in him.

37.13.0.en: The life of man is counted in days, but the days of Israel have no number [25].

37.14.0.en: The wise man inherits confidence in the midst of his people, and his name lives forever [26].

37.15.0.en: My son, test your soul while you live, and see what harms it, and do not give in to it [27].

37.16.0.en: For not everything is profitable to everyone, nor does every soul enjoy everything [28].

37.16.1.en: Father Gregory (the Great) said: [The venerable Gregory of Nazianzus has already taught us that the shepherd does not give one piece of advice to all. For one counsel is not suitable for all, since not all have the same character. The advice that benefits some may harm others. Like the pastures on which some animals feed while they are not fit for others. And the gentle whistle that calms the horse may excite the puppy. And the medicine that heals one person increases the diseases of another. And the food that nourishes the strong man destroys the little child.]

37.17.s.en: 4. Self-control and the sin of gluttony

37.17.0.en: 32 Do not be greedy for every pleasure, and do not pour yourself out upon foods. 33 For excess of eating makes the eater sick, and greediness reaches to colic. 34 Many have perished through greediness, but he who is content increases in life.

37.17.1.en: Truly all believers are called to avoid evil, so how much more does it befit us to choose the friend or counsellor who does not lack self-control, even in food.

37.17.2.en: Do not be greedy for every delicious food, and do not give yourself over to foods [29].

37.17.3.en: v Those who are free are not free according to their position, but those who are truly free in their life and character. For example, we may not call the famous and the rich free when they are wicked and fierce, for such are slaves of bodily passions. The freedom and blessedness of the soul are the fruit of true purity and contempt for temporal things[9].

37.17.4.en: St. Anthony the Great v We must control the belly and keep it under the direction of heaven. For God in the end will destroy all that belongs to the belly, as the Apostle says[10].

37.17.5.en: St. Clement of Alexandria v How do you see the posture of four-footed creatures? Their head is bent toward the earth, and they look to their belly, searching for the things that please them. But you, O man, your head is raised toward heaven, and your eyes look to the heights. So if you are defiled with the lusts of the flesh, and serve the pleasures of the belly and the lower pleasures, you by this [draw near to the beasts that have no reason, and become like them] (see Ps 49:12).

37.17.6.en: I set before you the care of another matter that befits you: "Seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth" (see Col 3:1). Rise above the accidents of the passing world, and learn from your bodily make-up, and make it the rule of your life: your city is heaven; your true homeland is the Jerusalem above, and your fellow citizens are the firstborn, whose names are written in the heavens[11].

37.17.7.en: St. Basil the Great v When the belly becomes the mistress of the body, she commands it and subjects it to her will, and instead of the way that leads to heaven she shows it the other way that brings it down to the abyss...

37.17.8.en: The passion of love of the belly is the worst of the passions. And the man who becomes subject to it, once he has borne its heavy yoke on his shoulders, does not accept to take a truce during his service to it. For this passion works in him day and night. It sends him wherever it wishes like a wretched servant, not on easy and smooth roads, but on roads full of stumbling stones, and into places where there are heavy losses. For the friend of the passions has no eyes with which to see the light...

37.17.9.en: The body is heavy by nature, but gluttony adds to it another weight... The animal, when it has filled its belly, leaves the rest of the food and does not store it... But man does not do that, because his desire is not filled when his belly is filled.

37.17.10.en: Eating out of lust is one thing, and eating out of need is another. He who eats out of fullness eats for the sake of the soul and not for the sake of the body. He nourishes his body so that it may be at every time ready to serve the soul....

37.17.11.en: It befits the disciple of Christ to flee from this foolish passion and not become a slave to his belly... The Apostle Paul said of the belly: "Whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame" (Phil 3:19)... The man who bows beneath that wicked passion cannot bear the yoke of discipleship to Christ[12].

37.17.12.en: St. Mar Philoxenus For excess of eating brings sickness, and gluttony leads to illness[13] [30].

37.17.13.en: Many have died of gluttony, but the man who is careful prolongs his life [31].

37.17.14.en: Gluttony is not only a sin that harms the soul, but it represents a danger even to the health of his body.

37.18.s.en: Choose for me friends and a counsellor, O searcher of hearts!

37.18.0.en: v Grant me friends and a counsellor in whom I see You manifested.

37.18.1.en: You are the searcher of hearts, and You know who they are that support me in the salvation of my soul.

37.18.2.en: I am no better than my brethren; I need one who will support me in You!

37.18.3.en: Grant my weakness to be a godly friend by Your grace.

37.18.4.en: Let Your grace work in me and in them, that together we may share in fellowship with You.

37.18.5.en: v Let Your Holy Spirit work in me, that I may touch Your Kingdom within me.

37.18.6.en: Grant me confidence and hope in the sanctification of my thoughts and my words, that I may walk in the truth under Your care.

37.18.7.en: Count me, together with my friends and counsellors, an instrument of righteousness for the sake of Your Kingdom.

37.18.8.en: May You lead my mind and my heart and also my belly, so that the passions of the flesh may not destroy me, nor my stomach enslave me, but that I may enjoy the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
